slides.title: Get started
slides.html:
Straw-and-pipe-cleaner stations: SSS, SAS, ASA, SSA, AAA. Each pair builds from the card and tries to make a triangle that does not match a neighbor's.

  • I can build triangles from three given parts and record whether every build comes out the same.
  • I can name the included angle of two sides and the included side of two angles, and explain why SSA and AAA are not tests.

geo.body:
Straw-and-pipe-cleaner stations: SSS, SAS, ASA, SSA, AAA. Each pair builds from the card and tries to make a triangle that does not match a neighbor's.

  • I can build triangles from three given parts and record whether every build comes out the same.
  • I can name the included angle of two sides and the included side of two angles, and explain why SSA and AAA are not tests.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html: some three-part recipes pin down a triangle and some don't. SSS, SAS and ASA are conjectures today. They are proved in 4.3, 4.4 and 4.10.

geo.title: Worked example
geo.prompt: Flashlight beams (informal, adapted from the airplane example on Jacobs p. 146).

steps.step: Tape a segment NT on the floor. Two students stand at N and T and aim flashlights inward at fixed angles, both on the same side of NT.
steps.reason: This fixes one side and the two angles at its ends.

steps.step: The beams cross at one point. Call it W.
steps.reason: Two straight beams that are not the same line cross at most once.

steps.step: A second team copies the same segment length and the same two angles, lays their tape on top of the first, and points the beams inward on the same side of segment NT.
steps.reason: Same recipe, same starting segment, same side.

steps.step: Their beams follow the same paths, so they cross at the same W.
steps.reason: The angles point the beams the same way.

steps.step: So this recipe (two angles and the side between them) seems to give only one triangle. We will prove it in 4.4.
steps.reason: Today it is a conjecture, not a theorem.

steps.step: Here are two triangles with corresponding angles marked equal as given information. All three pairs of angles are marked.
steps.reason: Given. The picture shows equilateral triangles, but the matching angles are told to us, not proved.

steps.step: A corresponding side is 2 in one and 5 in the other.
They cannot be congruent, because congruence preserves corresponding lengths.
steps.reason: Congruent shapes have equal matching lengths.

steps.step: Thus AAA does not guarantee congruence.

slides.title: Try it
slides.html: Use the controls. A drawing suggests a result; it is not a proof.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
Jordan says any three matching parts guarantee congruence.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Find and fix the error

'Any three matching parts are enough' is false. Where the parts sit matters, and AAA has no length at all.

geo.title: Common mistake
geo.prompt: Jordan says any three matching parts guarantee congruence.
geo.correction: 'Any three matching parts are enough' is false. Where the parts sit matters, and AAA has no length at all.

slides.title: Practice 1
slides.html:
Which angle is included between sides AB and AC?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Angle BAC.

Reveal second check

Both sides start at A, and A is the middle letter.

geo.title: Practice 1
geo.prompt: Which angle is included between sides AB and AC?
geo.check: Both sides start at A, and A is the middle letter.

slides.title: Practice 2
slides.html:
Which side is included between angles A and B?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Side AB.

Reveal second check

Its ends are the two angle corners. AC would sit between angles A and C instead.

geo.title: Practice 2
geo.prompt: Which side is included between angles A and B?
geo.check: Its ends are the two angle corners. AC would sit between angles A and C instead.

slides.title: Practice 3
slides.html:
Does matching all three angles (AAA) fix the size?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

No. The side 2 and side 5 equilateral triangles have matching angles but different lengths.

Reveal second check

A slide, turn or flip keeps a side of length 2 at length 2. It can never become 5.

geo.title: Practice 3
geo.prompt: Does matching all three angles (AAA) fix the size?
geo.solution: No. The side 2 and side 5 equilateral triangles have matching angles but different lengths.
geo.check: A slide, turn or flip keeps a side of length 2 at length 2. It can never become 5.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html:
Which three-part combinations failed to pin down one triangle?

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

SSA (sometimes two triangles) and AAA (same shape, any size).

Reveal second check

Name the givens and the theorem or definition used.
